name: Riso print look (with a live look switch)
what: Draws a three.js game as a risograph print: every object renders its ROLE into a small G-buffer, and one pass prints it as three spot inks (blue, pink, yellow) on paper through rotated halftone screens, with inked outlines, plate misregistration that grows with speed, uneven ink, paper grain, 8 ink sets and screen signals drawn in ink (freeze, dash, focus, hit, death, wipe). Game code asks for materials by role (mat(INK.ENEMY), mat(INK.WALL, MODE.WOOD)), so a look switch can redraw the same game in another look live; a plain lit look is included.
use_when: the game wants a printed, risograph, halftone, zine or screen-print look, or one game should offer several interchangeable visual styles chosen in settings.
good_for: Indoor or arena 3D games, first-person or third-person, where a strong graphic identity matters more than realism; games where colour must carry meaning (danger pink, yours yellow); offering a 'Look' choice in settings.
not_for: Adding onto an existing game's PBR materials without touching them (every material must come from mat()), orthographic cameras without a small change, photoreal games, games recorded mostly as small video clips (halftone dots bloat video).
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-riso-print, then follow HOW-TO-USE.md: create a look switch on ctx.view.renderer, give every mesh looks.mat(role, mode), and route the starter's draw through looks.view.render.
